# The type register

The 14 roles are the ramp. **80 declarations across 38 components do not use
one** — they compose type from primitives inline, `fontWeight` plus `fontSize`, the way CSS lets
you. This is the typographic twin of F-81, and it is the reason Gate A's type rule is not simply
"every text node has a style".

**Gate A's type rule:** a text node uses one of the 14 roles, **or** its combination appears in the
gaps table below. Anything else is a literal and a failure.

## Attach the role — 22 uses, 8 combinations

Weight, size and leading are identical to a role, so attaching it in Figma is **zero visual change**
and Gate B proves it on every one. The code still writes the primitives; that is F-81's question,
not this file's.

## No role — 58 uses, 29 combinations

Built faithfully in Figma with explicit values, by the owner's ruling of 21 Sep: inventing 29
more styles would turn a 14-step ramp into a 39-step list, and normalising the code to the nearest
role would be a restyle. A text node whose combination is here is **registered, not excused** — it is
the list the owner rules on, and the day a ruling comes it is one call to attach.

A `—` under Weight or Leading means the declaration does not set it, so the browser's own default
applies. Those are the ones most worth looking at: an unset line height on a 16px bold heading is
not a decision anybody made.
